articles.title: Fifa: Arsene Wenger considers standing against Gianni Infantino for presidency
articles.summary: Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering standing against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election in March.
articles.body:
Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering standing against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election.

For weeks, senior figures in European football have been hoping the Frenchman would run for the job, and he is now giving it serious thought.

Wenger is 77, leading to questions over whether he could provide long-term leadership for the sport.

But some of his supporters have told BBC Sport that they would be happy for him to win the election, then stand down before serving a full four-year term.

Infantino's position was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

But he retains support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.

However, that support could be tested if Wenger stands.

Fifa's head of global development would have the backing of Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino, and he has credibility throughout the footballing world.

Sources close to Wenger say he is yet to decide whether to stand, and they still believe Infantino is favourite to win a fourth and final term in next year's election.

The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino for the election in March is 18 November.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.

Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.

This month Fifa said "key documents" relating to Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup would be made available to members of its council, but they will have to travel to its Zurich base, and access will be under "strict protocols".

Last month Uefa gave football's world governing body until 2 November to release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and to answer questions relating to its decision-making.

That followed a council meeting at which Infantino apologised for the abandoned sell-off plot but failed to explain how the proposal was devised, asking that questions be submitted in writing.

Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."

Wenger has caused controversy at times in his Fifa role, notably for proposals such as biennial World Cups and a "daylight" offside law.

But he also has a global profile, including in Africa, where Infantino recently received a major re-election boost when receiving the backing of all 54 member national associations after promising an increase in funding.

Known as a champion of African players when in charge at Arsenal, Wenger's support of an expanded 48-team World Cup in order to drive development in countries beyond the game's traditional powers has been well received in the continent.

articles.title: Raúl, entre la ilusión y las dudas en un Oviedo con fracturas
articles.standfirst: Su llegada supone una bocanada de aire fresco, pero algunos sectores recelan de su falta de experiencia. El nuevo técnico se encontrará, además, con un problema social entre los dirigentes y una parte de la afición.
articles.summary: Su llegada supone una bocanada de aire fresco, pero algunos sectores recelan de su falta de experiencia. El nuevo técnico se encontrará, además, con un problema social entre los dirigentes y una parte de la afición.
articles.body: Cuando Raúl González Blanco se enfunde la ropa de entrenamiento del Real Oviedo y dirija su primera sesión de trabajo en las instalaciones de El Requexón, tendrá ante sí el primer gran reto de su carrera al frente de un primer equipo profesional. Aunque llega con la temporada iniciada y sin haber participado en la confección de la plantilla, no se encontrará con un equipo hundido ni con una situación que exija un milagro para alcanzar los objetivos anunciados. Eso sí, tendrá por delante una ardua tarea para convencer al oviedismo de su capacidad para sacar el máximo rendimiento a sus futbolistas, conseguir resultados y, sobre todo, lograr que Jesús Martínez, máximo responsable del Grupo Pachuca, se identifique con el estilo de juego que proponga. Cuando un equipo afronta un relevo en el banquillo, lo habitual es que atraviese una situación deportiva muy comprometida. Sin embargo, los dirigentes del Oviedo se han acostumbrado a cambiar de entrenador sin que el escenario resulte tan apurado como el de otros clubes que han tomado la misma decisión. Las Palmas, Eldense, Leganés, Cádiz, Albacete o Ceuta se han visto más alejados de sus expectativas y han apostado por un cambio de rumbo. El Oviedo, en cambio, se encuentra a una victoria de la zona de playoff y a dos del ascenso directo, antes de que se complete la decimotercera jornada. Desde el punto de vista clasificatorio, la situación no debería representar un gran hándicap para la leyenda madridista. Otra cosa bien distinta es el ambiente que rodea al equipo y la relación de la afición con sus dirigentes. Desde la llegada del Grupo Pachuca al accionariado del Real Oviedo hay una constante que no parece cambiar: la inestabilidad en los banquillos. Álvaro Cervera, Luis Carrión, Javi Calleja, Veljko Paunovic, Guillermo Almada y Julián Calero han desfilado por el Carlos Tartiere antes que Raúl, en una sucesión de proyectos interrumpidos que ha terminado por desgastar la confianza de una parte de la grada. Especialmente complicada fue la situación vivida hace trece meses, cuando el club decidió prescindir de Paunovic, con el equipo fuera de los puestos de descenso en Primera División, para apostar por el regreso de Carrión, que nunca contó con el visto bueno de buena parte de la afición. Aquella decisión marcó un punto de inflexión en la relación entre los seguidores y los dirigentes. Desde entonces, la contestación a la manera de gestionar el club por parte de Jesús Martínez no ha dejado de crecer. Si algo le sobra a Raúl es personalidad y experiencia para lidiar con situaciones de máxima exigencia. Su carrera como futbolista, una de las más brillantes del fútbol español, nunca estuvo exenta de críticas ni de ataques. Ahora deberá superar también el recelo que despierta su falta de experiencia al frente de un primer equipo profesional. Además, puede encontrarse con una de esas curiosas paradojas que rodean al fútbol: al margen de su pasión por el Oviedo, muchos aficionados azules simpatizan con el Real Madrid o el Barcelona. Es posible que el sector más barcelonista del oviedismo no contemple su llegada con el mismo entusiasmo que los seguidores madridistas, aunque el respaldo de estos últimos puede compensar sobradamente cualquier reticencia inicial. En sus primeras palabras como entrenador del Real Oviedo, Raúl ya dejó claro que le gusta el talento que encuentra en la plantilla azul. Las últimas semanas han permitido recuperar piezas llamadas a ser fundamentales, como Ilias Chaira y Estanis Pedrola, que tuvieron un papel protagonista en la victoria de Cádiz. Sin embargo, uno de sus principales problemas será encontrar un goleador que ponga remedio a la escasez ofensiva del equipo. Carlos Fernández parece estar cerca de regresar a las convocatorias, pero la baja de larga duración de Chris Ramos representa un contratiempo difícil de solucionar. También habrá que esperar para conocer el alcance exacto de la lesión de Dani Calvo, una pieza clave en el entramado defensivo de los azules. Ambas circunstancias deberán ser analizadas de cara al próximo mercado invernal, en el que el club tendrá la oportunidad de reforzar la plantilla y proporcionar al nuevo entrenador los recursos que considere necesarios. Antes de que arranque la era Raúl González en el banquillo del Tartiere, resulta inevitable que su nombramiento genere opiniones encontradas entre el oviedismo. Uno de sus grandes amigos en el fútbol, Fernando Hierro, ya vivió una experiencia similar cuando asumió las riendas del conjunto carbayón hace una década. Aunque el equipo no consiguió el ascenso ni alcanzó los puestos de playoff, quedó la sensación de que el malagueño había aportado cosas positivas a la entidad. Ahora, aquel futbolista al que Hierro bautizó en su día como “El Ferrari” quiere escribir su propia historia en Oviedo. Su desafío será repetir las buenas sensaciones que dejó su amigo, pero mejorando los resultados y, sobre todo, consiguiendo que la ilusión por su llegada termine imponiéndose a las dudas.

articles.title: Endrick y su futuro: "No me voy a lanzar al vacío, ya veremos qué pasa"
articles.standfirst: El brasileño compareció ante los medios de comunicación y abordó diferentes temas sobre su situación en el Real Madrid
articles.summary: El brasileño compareció ante los medios de comunicación y abordó diferentes temas sobre su situación en el Real Madrid
articles.body: Endrick ha hablado desde la concentración de la selección brasileña, donde sigue contando con la confianza del que también fuera su entrenador en el Real Madrid, Carlo Ancelotti. El atacante abordó diferentes cuestiones como su futuro y su situación actual en el conjunto blanco. El delantero acumula tan solo 140 minutos entre todas las competiciones, habiendo ingresado en el campo en un total de 7 partidos en los que sólo ha anotado un gol, ante la Roma en la remontada del duelo de Champions League. "Soy muy joven. Todavía no necesito lanzarme al vacío. Solo tengo 20 años y ya veremos qué pasa. Solo quiero jugar, quiero ser feliz, ayudar a mis compañeros… Marcar goles, dar asistencias, como lo hice en Lyon, que fue una de las mejores cosas que me han pasado y una de las épocas más felices de mi vida", explicó sobre su situación en el club blanco. Pese a ello, la prensa siguió insistiendo en su futuro y en una posible salida en el mercado invernal -que el propio Mourinho ya se ha encargado de negar en varias ocasiones- si sigue contando con las oportunidades justas. "No sé qué pasará en enero. Eso está en manos de Dios. Solo pido que se haga lo mejor para mi carrera. Pase lo que pase, pasará. Mantendré los pies en la tierra y daré lo mejor de mí. Madrid es una ciudad maravillosa, pero siempre haré todo lo posible por impulsar mi carrera", añadió. Sobre el trato de José Mourinho, entrenador del conjunto blanco, Endrick se mostró muy contundente. "Todos los días viene a verme y me pregunta cómo estoy, pero nunca sobre fútbol, siempre habla de mi vida personal. Valoro mucho eso. Es uno de los primeros entrenadores que llega, me saluda y me recibe con mucha calidez. Le estoy muy agradecido. Siempre lo daré todo por el Real Madrid, que está por encima de todo, pero con el cariño de Mourinho, doy aún más", expresó. Precisamente Mourinho ha insistido varias veces en público que es difícil que jugadores como Endrick o Carlos Espí tengan minutos con cierta asiduidad porque compiten en la misma posición con Kylian Mbappé, goleador y referencia del equipo. "Kylian el segundo mejor jugador del mundo en el último Balón de Oro. Siempre que tengo una oportunidad he dado lo mejor de mí. He estado entrando en los partidos cinco o diez minutos… y contra la Roma y el AEK Atenas aproveché esos momentos", contó.

articles.title: Nacho Palencia frena la euforia con el Real Madrid: "No podemos convertir lo normal en extraordinario"
articles.standfirst: Los tertulianos de La Tribu analizan el gran momento del conjunto blanco y debaten sobre su nivel respecto al Bayern, el PSG y el Barcelona
articles.summary: Los tertulianos de La Tribu analizan el gran momento del conjunto blanco y debaten sobre su nivel respecto al Bayern, el PSG y el Barcelona
articles.body: Ramón Álvarez de Mon, Nacho Palencia, María José Hostalrich, Nacho Labarga y Selene Melián han sido los tertulianos de este martes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marca por el parón de las selecciones y el nivel de algunos equipos de LaLiga. El buen momento del Real Madrid ha centrado buena parte del debate. El conjunto blanco atraviesa una dinámica positiva que ha despertado el optimismo sobre sus posibilidades de competir con los grandes clubes europeos. Sin embargo, no todos los tertulianos comparten el mismo entusiasmo. Nacho Palencia quiso poner los pies en el suelo y recordó que el nivel de exigencia del club madridista obliga a relativizar sus buenos resultados. "No podemos convertir lo normal en extraordinario. Que el Madrid compita bien los partidos, que le meta tres al Valencia o al Elche... Esto es lo normal", aseguró Palencia, que insistió en que las victorias del conjunto blanco deben analizarse teniendo en cuenta su potencial. "Que el Madrid pase por encima del 95% de los equipos de Europa y que sufra contra seis", añadió. El tertuliano también puso el foco en las dificultades que había atravesado el Real Madrid durante las últimas temporadas. "Hay que hacer ese ejercicio de por qué el Madrid ha estado dos años y medio sin conseguir ocho victorias consecutivas, sin ser un equipo fiable, reconocible y eficaz", reflexionó. Pese a su mensaje de prudencia, Palencia reconoció la mejoría del equipo. "Ahora está compitiendo muy bien, incluso mejor que el Barça con ese fútbol que siempre le ha ido muy bien", afirmó, antes de insistir en que no se debe exagerar el mérito de los resultados. "Lo extraordinario sería que el Betis fuera líder y hubiese ganado los 12 partidos", sentenció. Por su parte, Nacho Labarga destacó el crecimiento del conjunto blanco y lo situó entre los equipos más competitivos del continente, aunque todavía por detrás de dos grandes favoritos. "Creo que PSG y Bayern están un poquito por encima del Real Madrid, pero el Madrid les puede competir y en España es el equipo que mejor juega. Hace mes y medio nadie imaginaba esto", aseguró. En esa misma discusión intervino Jorge Liaño, que recordó la capacidad económica del club madridista y la calidad de su plantilla. "El Madrid ficha a tíos de 150 millones, claro que el Real Madrid les puede competir", afirmó. Más optimista se mostró Ramón Álvarez de Mon, que destacó la evolución del equipo y la estructura que ha conseguido encontrar. "El Madrid está en un gran momento, ha encontrado una estructura y ha ganado a su máximo rival", explicó. El tertuliano considera que el conjunto blanco todavía tiene que confirmar su crecimiento ante rivales de máxima exigencia, aunque ve motivos para confiar en su rendimiento. "Es una versión del Madrid que está a prueba, pero puede ser muy competitiva y muy estable ante equipos grandes", señaló. Además, Álvarez de Mon comparó la situación del Real Madrid con la del Barcelona y apuntó a las diferencias que observa entre ambos equipos. "Al Barcelona le hemos visto ciertas debilidades ante equipos de nivel que al Madrid, en esta versión, no se les han visto", concluyó.

articles.standfirst: No han conseguido elevar el nivel de la plantilla
articles.summary: No han conseguido elevar el nivel de la plantilla
articles.body: La media docena de incorporaciones realizadas por el Celta este verano no han supuesto, hasta la fecha, elevar el nivel de la plantilla. Más dudas que certezas hasta el momento en las incorporaciones. El equipo de Claudio Giráldez perdió dos futbolistas importantes como fueron Óscar Mingueza y Fer López, que estuvo media temporada, y no ha sido capaz de cubrir, hasta el momento, esas ausencias con solvencia. Sebastián Cáceres y Aleix Febas son los que están contando con más participación. El primero está cumpliendo en sus rotaciones en defensa, el segundo, del que se espera más, está siendo intermitente en su rendimiento, si bien es cierto que tuvo alguna complicación física en los primeros compases de la competición. Javi Galán está participando menos de lo esperado y en su vuelta a Vigo no acaba de ofrecer su mejor nivel. A su vez, Driouech no acaba de aportar lo que se esperaba del fichaje del verano en cuanto a inversión económica. En ambos casos se observa una mejoría en su rendimiento. Las otras dos incorporaciones no se pueden evaluar por su falta de presencia. Altay Bayindir no ha debutado y Faye apenas disputó el primer tiempo del partido ante el Athletic. Así las cosas, el director de fútbol, Marco Garcés, no descarta movimientos en el mercado invernal. La delicada economía del club tampoco permitirá excesos.

articles.title: Xaver Schlager at Nottingham Forest: Tough-tackling replacement for Elliot Anderson proves his worth to new club
articles.summary: Xaver Schlager has made more tackles than any other player in the Premier League and it helped Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City. With insight from his coaches past and present, Adam Bate examines why the unsung Austrian is quietly impressive...
articles.body:
The free transfer from Leipzig nipped in ahead of the £116m man that he has replaced in Forest's midfield and set Delap on the way to doubling the lead. Schlager is no Anderson but he has his own qualities and they made the difference at the weekend.

"It was a top team performance and it was a top performance by Xaver Schlager," said Forest boss Oliver Glasner in the press conference afterwards. He pointed out that "it must have been a fantastic performance" because City's midfielders are world-class.

Schlager was better. "He is so smart, anticipating and getting balls, one of the most for interceptions in the league. And he was physically so strong in his 50-50 balls. He always stayed on his feet and won these balls, because he can then play forward."

In fact, despite only coming on as a late substitute in Forest's opening defeat at home to Leeds , Schlager has made more tackles than any other player in the Premier League this season. It is a good illustration of the combative style that is his trademark.

Not every supporter has been enamoured by Schlager and perhaps that is inevitable given the team's underwhelming start to the season . When searching for explanations, new arrivals come under scrutiny and the 29-year-old Austrian is not one for the future.

But he has had a fine career. Before Leipzig, he worked with Glasner at Wolfsburg, having emerged at Red Bull Salzburg before that. Oscar Garcia spotted him in their feeder team Liefering, another of Glasner's former clubs, and gave him his senior debut.

"He had very good potential," Oscar tells Sky Sports . "Some players in midfield left and we wanted to give him the chance to play. In the structure of Red Bull there were other players ahead of him but we saw that he was a player who could do almost everything."

Not that the self-deprecating Schlager would admit that. Speaking in the summer, he acknowledged his limitations, revealing that "you will not see me too much" as he keeps the game simple. "I do the dirty things you do not recognise but someone has to do it."

Aside from his standout moment that was impossible to miss, that was exactly what he did in the win over City. In what was a particularly intense game, Schlager was the only outfield player on either side to win possession of the ball more times than he lost it.

As a result, the player who in that amusing introduction to the fans admitted that he was "not the quickest" and "not as skilful as some" is actually crucial. Maybe this was the key line? "The most important thing is I want to make my teammates around me better."

James McAtee, Schlager's partner in midfield for much of the season so far, is enjoying the best form of his Premier League career . Ryan Yates took the plaudits on his return to the starting line-up on Saturday. Schlager is a facilitator, a true team player.

Speaking to his former coach Oscar about him, he remains a huge admirer. "In midfield, he can have the ball, he can make the last pass, he can play with the left, he can play with the right, and he can recover the ball very well when the team is gegenpressing."

The passing aspect is not obvious but the statistics show that while his pass completion rate is 84.5 per cent, his expected completion rate is just 77.6 per cent given the difficulty of those passes under pressure. He is in the top 20 for overperformance on this metric.

In other words, Xaver Schlager is tidy on the ball and working incredibly hard off it. On Saturday, he ran 11.92 kilometres, more than anyone else on the pitch. He is not Elliot Anderson. But he is contributing. That big moment against City highlighted it perfectly.

articles.title: Chelsea not showing the consistency to get Champions League football this season, says Paul Merson
articles.summary: Chelsea have continued their inconsistent start to the season under Xabi Alonso, losing 1-0 to Sunderland to make it two league defeats in their last three games; the Blues are fifth in the Premier League table but in-form sides such as Everton, Bournemouth and Leeds could overtake them
articles.body:
Chelsea were poor in their loss to Regis Le Bris' side - who started the day bottom of the Premier League with just five points and one goal at home scored all season - and went down 1-0 thanks to Enzo Le Fee's first-half penalty.

As a result, Chelsea remain fifth in the Premier League table but in-form sides Everton and Bournemouth are now breathing down their necks.

Defeat to Leeds in their next game would move them behind the Whites as well, while their December schedule is tricky with Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa all to play the Blues before Christmas.

Read below for the Magic Man's thoughts about Chelsea's latest setback.

'If Chelsea don't get Champions League, it's a massive, massive failure'

I was very disappointed with Chelsea's performance at Sunderland. Very disappointed. They didn't play anywhere near the level they're capable of.

I'm not taking anything away from Sunderland at the same time, they were very good - and they played like they did last season when they were flying.

But this is Chelsea. You can't have one good week, one bad week at this football club.

They're renowned for winning trophies. Trophy after trophy. And don't get me wrong, it's been a long time since they won the Premier League. But, at the same time, you still expect a bit more consistency.

The consistency they're showing at the moment is not enough for top-five football. And Chelsea's aim is to get in the Champions League.

And if they don't get into the Champions League, it would be a massive, massive failure. A huge, massive failure.

Take a look at Brighton and Bournemouth this season. Everyone was saying that Thursday night football would catch up with them and it's a small squad. It's now less of an excuse for Chelsea, who are playing once a week.

I thought Xabi Alonso played into Sunderland's hands, if I'm being honest. He went there and showed them a little bit more respect than what I thought he should have.

They were bottom of the league with five points, and they were bottom of the league with five points for a reason.

Do you know what really worried me? Estevao was Chelsea's best player by a million miles last week against Manchester United - especially in the first half when they were really bad. They should have been 2-0 down at half-time.

But all of a sudden, they go to Sunderland and he's not playing. And he was missed. He's someone who can take the ball up the pitch for them.

Alonso had to pick Estevao, play the same team they put out against Man Utd and get him to run with the ball. Instead, he tried to make it tight, and make sure they don't get beat over winning the game.

'Chelsea stars are just waiting for someone else to start playing first'

At Chelsea, these big star players are all waiting for someone else to do it before they start playing. That's the feeling I get at the moment.

It's like: 'When someone else does a bit of magic and then we go one or two up, then I'll start playing'. They need to start producing when it's 0-0.

And Levi Colwill got found out at Sunderland. He got absolutely ripped to shreds by Brian Brobbey.

You're not going to fight Brobbey, you're not going to beat him up, you're not quicker than him. And he tried to prove that he was - and just kept on getting done. That was worrying for me - and it was no surprise that he came off at half-time.

Because after half-time, Brobbey didn't do much. Chelsea made sure he wasn't allowed to fight with people. They dropped off him and they didn't let Brobbey feel anyone - which makes a massive, massive difference.

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup: England Wheelchair score record points total against home nation Australia to reach final
articles.summary: England Wheelchair beat Australia 86-18 to reach fifth successive Rugby League World Cup final; Rob Hawkins led the charge for his side with a stunning 30-point performance; England face France in World Cup final in Wollongong on Friday
articles.body:
The game was all but over at half-time as England held a 40-6 lead, with Rob Hawkins leading the charge for his side with a stunning 30-point performance in his side's dominant victory.

The win means the defending World Cup champions will face France in the final in Wollongong on Friday, with a chance to claim their third World Cup title.

Mason Billington - who picked up Player of the Match - opened the scoring in just the third minute of the contest with a try, before Hawkins added two of his own and back Joe Coyd got in on the act to put England in firm control with a 30-0 lead after just 24 minutes.

Diab Karim eventually got the host nation on the scoresheet with a converted try, but their joy was short-lived after Billington went over twice to seal his hat-trick before half-time.

Interchanges Jack Brown and Nathan Collins scored three tries between them in the opening 10 minutes of the second half before Hawkins struck twice more to put England out of reach.

Karim and Dan Antsey went over for consolations just after the hour mark, but tries from Chris Haynes and the captain Lewis King put the finishing touches on a sensational victory for the two-time World Champions.

England Wheelchair rugby league captain Lewis King:

I don't want to put a number on it but we are proud of that performance, we were super disciplined in how we wanted to play. We had a game plan and we executed it. I am super proud."

"I am grateful for the opportunity [to be captain] and I don't want to take putting this badge on as an opportunity because you don't know how many times you will get to do it.

"I am excited for the opportunity. The culture of this team is teammates we are like brothers. I am looking forward to Friday.

"When we meet France, it is always down to the finer details and margins, so I won't be thinking about France, we will be focused on us."

articles.title: Quadri Liameed no jugará en Elda por el protocolo de conmociones
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista nigeriano fue sustituido contra la Real Sociedad B por mareos
articles.summary: El centrocampista nigeriano fue sustituido contra la Real Sociedad B por mareos
articles.body: Quadri Liameed, centrocampista nigeriano del Sabadell, no jugará el partido de este domingo en Elda porque se ha vuelto a activar el protocolo de conmociones. Quadri, imprescindible en la zona ancha arlequinada, tuvo que ser sustituido a los 12 minutos del partido de este lunes contra la Real Sociedad B en la Nova Creu Alta (0-0), justo después del minuto de homenaje a Jesús de Miguel. Algunos medios apuntaron a que había pedido el cambio porque se había emocionado, ya que en la última jornada también había sido protagonista por un golpe muy fuerte en la cabeza. Quadri cayó inconsciente sobre el campo del Albacete (2-1)y tuvo que ser evacuado en ambulancia, entre escenas de angustia y de preocupación. El Sabadell ha descartado este martes que Quadri pidiera el cambio contra la Real Sociedad B porque se emocionara y que fue porque sintió "un poco de molestar" desde el inicio del partido. Fue sustituido por precaución y siguió el resto del partido desde el banquillo, junto a sus compañeros. El club de la Nova Creu Alta también ha detallado que el su dorsal '22' ha pasado bien la noche y que no ha notado "nada extraño". Aun así, el protocolo de conmociones estipula que ahora debe estar siete días sin hacer deporte y, por lo tanto, será baja para el encuentro del domingo en casa del Eldense. Será su primera ausencia, después de ser titular en los 13 partidos jugados hasta la fecha. Su técnico, Ferran Costa, explicó después del empate con la Real Sociedad B que Quadri le pidió el cambio porque no se encontraba bien, porque se mareaba. "Ha sido una semana muy difícil porque solo ha podido entrenar un día. Quiero ser prudente, pero la hostia que se llevó fue brutal. Lo ha querido intentar. Así son estos jugadores. Si a mí me meten una hostia así no me levanto en tres semanas, pero él ha querido forzar", aseguró.

articles.title: Michael Carrick future: Man Utd head coach position increasingly in doubt with Mauricio Pochettino open to talks
articles.summary: Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick's position under increasing threat, but no final decision; Sky Sports News understands Mauricio Pochettino would be open to a discussion with Man Utd if he approached by club; it is thought the cost of buying him out of his USA contract is around £7m
articles.body:
CEO Omar Berrada and Wilcox are due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco for a scheduled meeting on Wednesday, with the duo to discuss the findings of their season review and give their recommendations on Carrick's future, while also assessing their options.

Sky Sports News has been told that, as yet, no final decision has been taken on Carrick's Old Trafford future.

With Pochettino open to talks with United, it is thought the cost of buying him out of his contract with his current job as USA head coach would be around £7m.

The former Argentina defender recently extended his deal with the USA until 2030 and is preparing to face Haiti in the Nations League quarter-finals.

In the past, United have had discussions with Pochettino on at least two occasions regarding the United job.

Carrick arrived at the club's training ground on Tuesday morning as the club carries out a full review of the team's performance so far this season , led by director of football Jason Wilcox.

Carrick was given a reprieve following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago, with the bosses keen to give him a further three matches to try to turn the team's fortunes around.

But the pressure has continued to mount on Carrick after an eighth straight Premier League match without a win. There are now real doubts about whether he will be in charge of the team which goes to Anfield to play Liverpool the weekend after next.

The United hierarchy is determined that results have to improve, but they want to be sure about which direction to take the team before any action is taken.

If they decide to remove Carrick from his position, they want to avoid having an interim head coach take over, but as yet, there have been no substantive talks with other potential candidates.

Sky Sports News understands the club's hierarchy are planning to use the international break to fully evaluate the season so far and reassess their options.

Carrick and the players have all had Monday off after rescuing a late point against Villa on Sunday, but the head coach and his staff are due back into Carrington on Tuesday.

With most players away on international duty and no first-team training sessions planned in the coming days, that has bought some breathing space for a full re-evaluation of the season.

One win in 11 games, 30 goals conceded so far in all competitions, the worst record of any team in the top-five European leagues, and a worst-ever start to a Premier League season has ramped up the pressure on Carrick.

Those problems have outweighed the positivity brought about by the comebacks of the last two matches.

It is thought the United hierarchy feel Carrick over-achieved last season, with a third-placed League finish earning Champions League football.

But it is equally clear the bosses are adamant that the club's current crop of players have woefully under-achieved so far this season.

Sky Sports News understands there are three key reasons why United are not rushing a decision over the head coach position - all of which have given Carrick an extended stay of execution.

Firstly, the supporters are not singing for him to be sacked. It is unlikely that will ever happen, such is the affection of the fanbase for a legendary player who won 11 major trophies with United, including the Champions League and five Premier League titles.

As such, the pressure to change the boss which other clubs often experience from the stands has not materialised at Old Trafford.

Secondly, there is a feeling in the boardroom that Carrick and his coaching staff still retain the support of the players.

Despite the chaotic nature of the last two games, they have produced a Champions League win against Roma and a draw against a good Villa side - with notable comebacks in both.

As such, the assessment seems to be that the players have not downed tools, and they are still fighting for Carrick.

Thirdly, United's bosses remain unconvinced at this stage that changing the head coach will solve the team's problems.

If they did believe that, they could have already made a move to sack Carrick and appoint a candidate such as Julian Nagelsmann or Eddie Howe - both of whom are out of work, available, and thought to be keen to talk to United if a vacancy becomes available.

'It doesn't matter who's in charge at Man Utd'

Sky Sports News chief reporter Kaveh Solhekol :

"The club needs to become Manchester United again. They need to turn into a club who are capable of winning the title regularly, winning the European Cup again.

"It doesn't matter who's in charge, in my opinion. You could have Carlo Ancelotti, Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp. But with the present ownership structure, I don't think things are going to change.

"You could bring in another manager but you would just paper over the cracks. We're talking about a club that used to rub shoulders with Barcelona and Real Madrid.

"If things carry on as they are at the moment, they'll be rubbing shoulders with Lincoln and QPR. There's a circus around the club, everyone talking about what's going wrong and how it can be changed.

"But I think most Man Utd fans think that unless you change the owners, nothing is going to change."

articles.title: Las Palmas deja atrás los problemas tras tres victorias consecutivas
articles.standfirst: Encadena la mejor racha de la temporada y se aleja de los puestos de descenso
articles.summary: Encadena la mejor racha de la temporada y se aleja de los puestos de descenso
articles.body: La UD Las Palmas parece haber dejado atrás los fantasmas que amenazaban con complicar su temporada. El conjunto amarillo ha encadenado tres victorias consecutivas, su mejor racha del curso, que le ha permitido recuperar sensaciones y tomar distancia respecto a los puestos de descenso. Los triunfos ante la Real Sociedad B, todavía con Juan Manuel Rodríguez al frente del equipo, y contra el Real Oviedo y el Eldense, ya con Albert Sánchez en el banquillo, han supuesto un importante punto de inflexión para los grancanarios. Esta reacción llega después de tocar fondo. Las Palmas atravesaba un momento más que delicado, con un solo punto sumado en sus cinco encuentros anteriores. Además, había dejado una imagen preocupante en partidos como el disputado en Mallorca o en casa frente al Castellón. La falta de resultados y las malas sensaciones habían encendido las alarmas, pero el equipo ha sabido cambiar la dinámica en el momento más necesario. Tres victorias que no solo se traducen en puntos, sino también en confianza y tranquilidad para afrontar los próximos compromisos. Buena parte de este cambio de rumbo coincide con la llegada de Albert Sánchez, tercer entrenador del equipo en lo que va de temporada. El técnico ha comenzado su etapa de la mejor manera posible, con dos triunfos en sus dos primeros encuentros. Pese a ello, Sánchez mantiene la cautela y es consciente de que todavía queda trabajo por hacer: "Estamos en ese proceso de mejora, todo parte de estar sólidos en defensa y solo nos falta ajustar cuatro cosas", reconoció tras el último partido. Un mensaje que refleja la intención de consolidar esta mejoría y convertir la reacción actual en el inicio de una dinámica positiva.

articles.title: El Atlético se mueve para fichar a un 3: Cardona, sobre la mesa
articles.standfirst: La prioridad para enero es incorporar a un lateral que compita con Grimaldo tras no cerrarse a Tagliafico en verano. El zurdo del Villarreal, que acaba contrato, encaja en el perfil deseado
articles.summary: La prioridad para enero es incorporar a un lateral que compita con Grimaldo tras no cerrarse a Tagliafico en verano. El zurdo del Villarreal, que acaba contrato, encaja en el perfil deseado
articles.body: Aunque aún queda algo más de mes y medio para que se abra el mercado de invierno, el Atlético ya tiene clara su prioridad: un lateral izquierdo que compita el puesto a un Grimaldo sin un relevo específico en la plantilla. Tanto es así que Mateu Alemany ya se mueve para fichar a un 3 después de que la operación de Tagliafico no llegara a culminarse el pasado verano. Cabe recordar que el titular de la Argentina campeona del mundo en Qatar en 2022 llegó a tener todo cerrado con el Atlético en el día que expiraba mercado, pero faltaría el último paso. Pese a que Mateu Alemany había acordado las condiciones tanto con el Olympique de Lyon como con el propio Tagliafico, finalmente finalmente no habría luz verde desde el Metropolitano. En este sentido, su llegada estaba supeditada a las salidas de Giménez, Lemar, Carlos Martín u Obed Vargas en las que se trabajaba en paralelo. Pero, pese a conseguirse las de los dos primeros (el canterano se iría a Croacia ya con el mercado nacional cerrado), no se concretarían en los términos más deseados por el Atlético. De ahí que tras valorar la situación, se optara por no seguir adelante con el argentino e inscribir con ficha del primer equipo a Dani Martínez, central del filial que desde entonces se reciclaría en lateral para ejercer de sustituto de Grimaldo. Un 'parche' que el paso de los meses no ha hecho más que evidenciar la necesidad de doblar el puesto con un especialista. Por eso Alemany no ha dejado de peinar el mercado en estos meses. Eso sí, si Tagliafico se presentaba entonces como una buena opción por su amplia y probada experiencia, por su predisposición a recalar en el Atlético (la caída del fichaje a última hora le supuso un mazazo tras verse con las maletas hechas) y por el encaje de su ficha en la masa salarial rojiblanca, ahora la mirada del director de fútbol profesional masculino se ha ampliado a más frentes. Sin perder la perspectiva de que el elegido no vendría con la vitola de titular sino como un lateral que pueda aumentar la competencia a Grimaldo y darle descansos de garantías sin que Simeone se vea obligado a recursos como el de desplazar a Hancko a la banda, Mateu trabaja en un futbolista fiable, pero de bajo coste. Un perfil en el que encajaría una de las opciones que ya tiene sobre su mesa: Sergi Cardona. Con su contrato en el Villarreal expirando en junio, su salida en enero no acarrearía una excesiva inversión, siendo uno de los aspectos que se tienen en cuenta en el Metropolitano. El otro es que a sus 27 años ya cuenta con la madurez suficiente para desenvolverse en la élite. No en vano, a lo largo de sus cuatro temporadas en Primera (una en Las Palmas) ya supera el centenar de presencias, al margen de sus 12 participaciones en la Champions, con gol incluido. Por ahí viene otro factor que invita a incluirlo en la agenda, pues su estilo ofensivo se asemeja al de Grimaldo. Basta con atender a sus cifras en el Villarreal, con cuatro dianas y 12 asistencias en 90 partidos por más que en el presente curso alterne sus apariciones con Carlos Romero. Sin olvidar que fue uno de los estandartes del último ascenso de Las Palmas, llamando ya por entonces la atención de un Atlético que vuelve a tenerlo en la recámara como una opción en estudio.

articles.title: El Castellón pierde a tres jugadores en la nueva ventana FIFA
articles.standfirst: Orozco, Rego y Saipi no estarán frente al Valladolid
articles.summary: Orozco, Rego y Saipi no estarán frente al Valladolid
articles.body: Las convocatorias internacionales vuelven a afectar al Castellón de cara a su compromiso liguero del fin de semana, que será el de su regreso a la competición tras el aplazamiento de su choque frente al Eibar. Así, los albinegros acudirán a su próximo partido, en Valladolid, sin tres jugadores citados por sus selecciones: Maty Orozco, Rodrigo Rego y Amir Saipi. Estos jugadores repiten convocatoria tras ser llamados hace un mes y medio en la primera ventana FIFA de la temporada. El colombiano, además, está sancionado por su expulsión frente al Burgos, por lo que se iba a perder el choque del José Zorrilla de todas formas. El centrocampista cafetero tiene dos amistosos frente a Chile los días 13 y 17 de noviembre, en su segunda convocatoria como internacional absoluto. En las mismas fechas, Rego jugará también encuentros amistosos con la selección sub-21 de Portugal ante Inglaterra y Noruega. Finalmente, el portero Saipi afronta dos compromisos de la Liga de Naciones con Kosovo el 14 y el 17 frente a Israel e Irlanda respectivamente. La ausencia de Orozco, titular indiscutible en el Castellón, provocará al menos un cambio en el once inicial albinegro en el José Zorrilla, con el interrogante de quién va a acompañar a Diego Barri en el doble pivote. Álvaro Martín y Jari Vlak son los aspirantes a ese puesto. Quien podría volver a las convocatorias es otro de los hombres importantes del cuadro albinegro, Ousmane Camara, que se ha perdido un mes y medio de competición debido a una lesión.

articles.title: Lucas Rosa, en el radar de Ancelotti para Brasil
articles.standfirst: El lateral brilla en el Ajax y ya ha despertado el interés del seleccionador
articles.summary: El lateral brilla en el Ajax y ya ha despertado el interés del seleccionador
articles.body: El jugador brasileño Lucas Rosa atraviesa sin duda por el mejor momento en su carrera. A sus 26 años de edad, poco a poco se está asentando en el Ajax, equipo en el que ya lleva año y medio desde su salida del Real Valladolid. De hecho, el defensor ha ido progresando hasta convertirse en la actualidad en pieza fundamental para el entrenador Míchel Sánchez. Lucas no sólo se ha hecho con un puesto en el once, sino que destaca en el vistoso estilo de juego habitual del técnico español, donde los laterales son muy importantes tanto en ataque como en defensa. En estos primeros meses de la temporada actual, el brasileño ya ha estado presente en ocho de los 12 partidos de la Eredivisie, en la que la parte alta de la tabla está muy igualada, con cinco equipos en sólo tres puntos de distancia, siendo el conjunto de Ámsterdam tercero a un punto del líder, el PSV. El jugador, elegido el MVP de su equipo en algunos partidos, ha disputado el 65% de los minutos en Liga, aumentando esa cifra incluso en la Conference League, donde recientemente participó en una escandalosa goleada (1-6) ante el Midtjylland danés. El crecimiento del futbolista en este tiempo no está pasando desapercibido para nadie, incluido para un Carlo Ancelotti, seleccionador brasileño, que ya tiene su nombre apuntado en la agenda como posibilidad en futuras convocatorias de la absoluta. No en vano, Lucas ya participó con las categorías inferiores de la 'canarinha' cuando sólo tenía 16 años. Ahora, su progresión le puede llevar más pronto que tarde a estrenarse en una lista y poder debutar con el combinado de su país. También está atento a la situación del defensa su anterior club, el Real Valladolid. La explosión de Lucas Rosa y su mejoría continua le podría dar un rédito mayor del que obtuvo al traspasar al jugador al Ajax por tres millones de euros fijos en el mercado de invierno del año pasado. Y es que el club blanquivioleta se quedó con un 10% de una posible plusvalía, por lo que si la entidad neerlandesa lo vendiera en un futuro, el Pucela obtendría una cantidad que ayudaría a mejorar sus problemas económicos.

articles.title: Saël Kumbedi: "Ser entrenado por Zidane alegra el corazón"
articles.standfirst: El defensa del Wolfsburgo mostró su sorpresa por ser convocado por el seleccionador francés
articles.summary: El defensa del Wolfsburgo mostró su sorpresa por ser convocado por el seleccionador francés
articles.body: Saël Kumbedi es el hombre de moda en Francia. El jugador del Wolfsburgo, de la segunda división alemana, fue convocado por Zidane para acudir a la selección francesa en este parón de ligas debido a los partidos de la Nations League. "Ser convocado por Zidane alegra el corazón. Ya había coincidido con él antes. Había venido a dar consejos porque yo jugaba con su hijo Elyaz. Pero este caso, ser entrenador por Zidane es algo formidable", comentó el futbolista de 21 años tras hacerse oficial su convocatoria. "Me estaba preparando para incorporarme a la sub-21, así que estaba en casa esperando el taxi cuando recibí una llamada en la que me comunicaron que iba a estar con la selección absoluta. ¡Me puse contentísimo", dijo Kumbedi ante los medios. "Me he preparado para esto. No sabía que esto llegaría tan pronto, pero siempre lo tuve presente en un rincón en mi cabeza. Ahora me toca a mí aprovechar mi oportunidad. Se podría decir que es un sueño hecho realidad, no es un fin en sí mismo. Hay que seguir trabajando y mantener la cabeza sobre los hombros", concluía el jugador.

articles.title: England: James Hill called up as cover for Ezri Konsa for Croatia Nations League game
articles.summary: Bournemouth defender James Hill is added to the England squad for Thursday's Nations League match against Croatia at Wembley.
articles.body:
Bournemouth defender James Hill has been called up to the England squad for the first time.

The 24-year-old centre-back has been added to Thomas Tuchel's squad after Arsenal's Ezri Konsa was ruled out of Thursday's Nations League match against Croatia at Wembley.

Konsa was substituted after sustaining a knee injury in the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday, but played all 90 minutes of the win over Hull on Saturday.

He will return to full training this week, before England's game against Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

On Sunday Dan Burn replaced centre-back Marc Guehi , who withdrew with a hip injury.

Hill has played every minute of Bournemouth's Premier League season and has featured in every game of their inaugural Europa League campaign.

He joined Bournemouth from Fleetwood for an undisclosed fee in January 2022.

Having made only 24 appearances in his first three and a half years with the club, Hill became a regular last season as Bournemouth achieved their highest top-flight finish of sixth.

Bournemouth, who are on an eight-match winning run in all competitions, are seventh in the Premier League.

articles.title: Aaron Collins: Wales add MK Dons striker with Kieffer Moore out
articles.summary: Wales have called up MK Dons striker Aaron Collins for this month's Nations League matches following Wrexham frontman Kieffer Moore's withdrawal due to injury.
articles.body:
Wales have called up uncapped MK Dons striker Aaron Collins for this month's Nations League matches following Wrexham frontman Kieffer Moore's withdrawal due to injury.

Moore, 34, left the field during Wrexham's 1-1 Championship draw with Wolves on Saturday.

Wales have not specified what kind of injury the 57-cap forward has sustained.

He is replaced in the Wales squad by Collins, who has scored 17 goals in 16 games across all competitions for League One side Dons this season, including four goals in a game against Doncaster last month.

The 29-year-old former Newport County player joins Craig Bellamy's squad for concluding Group A4 games in Norway and at home to Portugal.

Newport-born Collins has played for 10 different - mainly lower league - clubs since leaving Rodney Parade for Wolverhampton Wanderers in 2016.

Wales, who are looking to preserve their place in the Nations League's top tier, face Norway in Oslo on Saturday before finishing their campaign at home against Portugal next Tuesday.

Wales are third in Group A4, with their only win from four matches so far coming against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway in Cardiff last month.

Bellamy is without midfielder Jordan James but has influential Leeds pair Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon back, along with Cardiff playmaker Rubin Colwill.

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live Sports Extra, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Bellamy's side could still finish in second, third or fourth place.

A top-two spot would take Wales to the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027.

Finishing third would mean a relegation play-off against a League B team in March, while finishing bottom of the group would result in either a relegation play-off or direct relegation, depending on the ranking with other League A groups.

articles.title: Antony agradece el apoyo del beticismo "incluso en los momentos en los que las cosas no salen"
articles.standfirst: El brasileño no termina de encontrar su mejor versión esta temporada
articles.summary: El brasileño no termina de encontrar su mejor versión esta temporada
articles.body: Antony no está cómodo y se le nota. El brasileño salió contrariado el pasado domingo del Martínez Valero y no es la primera vez esta temporada. Fue uno de los primeros cambios de Manuel Pellegrini, como en Dortmund y también ante el Málaga. Su momento físico y futbolístico están un punto por debajo de un Betis que vuela en LaLiga y sorprende en la Champions. El brasileño quiere volver a ser el mismo que deleitó a la afición del Betis y es el primero en reconocer que algo no funciona. "Quiero agradecer de corazón a todos los béticos por el cariño y el apoyo que me están dando, incluso en los momentos en los que las cosas no salen como uno desea. Siento vuestro cariño y solo puedo deciros que os quiero muchísimo", han sido las palabras que Antony publicó en una de sus stories horas después del partido disputado frente al Elche. Pelegrini declaró recientemente que la confianza en el jugador es "máxima". Necesita recuperar la calma. Hace tiempo que superó los problemas de pubalgia que le lastraron el curso pasado y el técnico chileno señaló en otra ocasión uno de los motivos del irregular rendimiento del extremo. "Creo que Antony tiene mucha autoexigencia. Está corriendo mucho y recuperando balones. Igual por exceso de ansiedad le está faltando en los metros finales, pero llegarán los goles", aseguró el míster. Antony se quedó en el banquillo en el partido frente al Barcelona, pero ha participado en el resto de compromisos oficiales del equipo esta temporada. Un total de 1.005 minutos en el césped, repartidos en once jornadas de LaLiga y cuatro de Champions Y solo registra una asistencia, precisamente en la máxima competición continental ante el Oporto.

articles.title: Foreign coaches in the Championship: Why working in England's second tier is a target for top managers from abroad
articles.summary: With insight from talking to Miron Muslic, Vitor Campelos and Sergej Jakirovic, Adam Bate assesses the lure of the Championship for foreign coaches and why many in Europe now see it as the most appealing route to the ultimate goal of becoming a Premier League manager
articles.body:
This is the famous Championship, offering raucous crowds, potential riches and a route to the Premier League. That is what has drawn the other eight - coaches from Belgium, Italy, France, Germany, Sweden, Switzerland and two from Portugal - with more waiting.

Each of these men are first-time managers in English football and while not all of them will find success here, the odds are in favour of at least one of them being able to call themselves a Premier League manager once the Championship season is concluded.

Top coaches are alive to the possibilities in England's second tier. It was a privilege to attend two games with Portuguese coach Vitor Campelos recently to gain a greater appreciation not just of the game here but its appeal to those working elsewhere.

Campelos has offers at home and abroad, the chance to continue his top-flight coaching career on the continent is there. But the lure of the British game took him on a fact-finding mission both north and south of the border. It proved an illuminating trip.

Watching games with genuine experts is always insightful. Campelos, who has coached three different teams in Portugal's top division and won the title in Slovenia earlier this year, was impressed by Wolves' shape at Bristol City but wanted to see more rotations.

He enjoyed Scott Twine's stunning free-kick at Ashton Gate and shared tales of how he would empower his own players by sending them off in groups to devise set-piece routines for the weekend. "They are so much more engaged when it is their own idea."

At Pride Park, Campelos noted how Bolton were able to pull Derby around the pitch. "Look at the space every time for Ruben Rodrigues in the half spaces." His compatriot opened the scoring soon after. But the Championship is not always so predictable.

Derby produced an unlikely second-half comeback and won the game 3-1 with only 30 per cent of the possession. "Football is amazing," concluded Campelos. The crowd of 27,536 watching a team winless in 10 games was a reminder of English football's depth.

For context, Derby are currently 43rd in the pyramid but would be the fourth-best supported team in Portugal by a wide margin. Campelos points out the vocal away support at Pride Park too. Bolton took 3,000 fans to Pride Park for the evening kick-off.

The pull of the atmosphere might seem overly romantic but it is real. Miron Muslic has less reason than most to eulogise the uniqueness of English football given that he is the coach of Schalke , the club with the biggest away following in world football last season.

But even he remembers his time with Plymouth Argyle fondly in part because of the rhythms of English football, the feeling that the crowd were truly a part of the contest. It is special. "Players always ask me about the Championship," Muslic tells Sky Sports .

"And I always tell everyone the same thing. You have to experience this. You guys have to go to England and sign for, hopefully a Premier League club, but if not Premier League then the Championship, because the football is just pure. And I love the atmosphere."

Muslic is an animated man at all times but he becomes particularly excited at the recollection of that precise noise when the ball hits the net in an English stadium. "Always after you score the goal," he says. "This first [roar]. It is only like this in England."

There is noise in Germany. It is often more spectacular with eye-catching choreography and a relentless chanting that continues regardless of the fortunes of the team. "It is organised here," says Muslic. It is neither better nor worse but it is noticeably different.

Fans are less likely to react spontaneously to the action. "That is the biggest difference. The guys at Plymouth, they celebrated a tackle . And one aerial duel and we smashed the ball over there and everybody was like, 'Yeah, ******* hell!' That is typically English."

Muslic was not quite able to keep Plymouth up after taking over in tough circumstances from Wayne Rooney. But, bolstered by an FA Cup win over Liverpool, he enhanced his reputation sufficiently to earn the move to Schalke and is now in the Bundesliga.

The Championship brings eyeballs and opportunity. Muslic had to move to make it to a major European league but others are able to use it to take a more direct route to the top. Sergej Jakirovic certainly proved that with the job he did at Hull City last season.

Hull were unfancied having only just stayed up the previous season. But Jakirovic was able to mastermind their promotion via the play-offs. He is acutely aware that he had little chance of getting one of those 20 jobs but now he is a Premier League manager.

"I do not know too many coaches who start like I do, in the academy, and then step by step, you come here. Mr Acun [Ilicali] gave me my opportunity and then with this promotion, you are now in the Premier League," the Bosnian coach tells Sky Sports .

"It is a big privilege and I am very proud of this, my journey. And this is the reason why I will give everything to be successful. It is not easy to get the chance, to get the job, especially from my country. But you have to use your moments also, your opportunity."

Campelos and many more like him and out there hoping to get their own opportunity soon and the success of Jakirovic and others shows that there are bright coaches with big ideas capable of making an impact even if the Brexit-regulations are a complication.

Despite only one third of Championship coaches coming from continental Europe, they account for five of the top eight. When it comes to progressive football, it can be easier to demonstrate that skill abroad than working in England's lower leagues.

Campelos, for example, can point to his Celje side in Slovenia ranking 26th out of over 1000 clubs across 68 leagues in a recent CIES Football Observatory report calculating the 'ability to dictate games' domestically. Desirable qualities for ambitious owners.

The Portuguese is insightful on matters of coaching, tactics and the psychology behind team cohesion. He has been of interest to two Championship clubs and, for now, is ready to wait for his chance.

For coaches, as with players, the dream is the Premier League. Many are realising that the Championship is the way to reach that goal.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs after Week 10
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included are each player's numbers through the air and on the ground, their game's outcome, and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight the quality of the opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F. Those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 23-of-43, 252 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, -1 yard Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Texas) Week 10 Outcome: Loss (20-34)

Despite his fifth 250-yard, two-touchdown performance of the season, Austin Simmons was unable to lead Missouri to victory over Texas, and the Tigers have now dropped two of their last three games.

The Ole Miss transfer still ranks among the SEC leaders in passing yards (2,204, fourth) and passing touchdowns (18, second), though his 61.8 percent completion rate lags behind and his 20 incompletions on Saturday were a season high.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 16-of-20, 214 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 12 carries, 87 yards, 1 TD Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Oregon State) Week 10 Outcome: Win (42-21)

Brad Jackson had 3,224 passing yards, 744 rushing yards and 38 total touchdowns during the 2025 season, and he was arguably the best mid-major quarterback in the country to stay put rather than entering the transfer portal.

He leads the new-look Pac-12 in completion percentage (68.3) and passer rating (159.9), and while the Bobcats are 5-4 on the year, he has now led them to quality wins over North Texas and Oregon State.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 17-of-25, 210 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 26 yards Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (UTSA) Week 10 Outcome: Win (60-29)

Caden Veltkamp threw for 3,641 yards and 24 touchdowns last season, but he also led the nation with 17 interceptions, and he has taken a significant step forward this season.

He leads the AAC in completion percentage (71.6) and passing touchdowns (27), and has slashed his interception rate from 3.3 to 1.5 percent, throwing just five picks through nine games. Thursday's performance came against a 7-1 UTSA team pushing for a spot in the AP Top 25.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 11-of-16, 303 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 19 carries, 88 yards, 3 TD Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Texas Tech) Week 10 Outcome: Loss (48-53)

For the fifth time this season, Michael Hawkins Jr. tallied at least four total touchdowns, and his 303 passing yards on Saturday were his second-highest total of the year and came against a good Texas Tech defense.

His 31 touchdowns rank second among all FBS players, trailing only Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker (33), and his rushing talents have helped open up the passing game for an FBS-leading 10.9 yards per attempt.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 9-of-15, 186 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 28 yards, 1 TD Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Ole Miss) Week 10 Outcome: Win (42-7)

Georgia built a 28-0 lead in the first half on Saturday and leaned heavily on the running game to get to the finish line, with Gunner Stockton attempting just 15 passes against the team's 48 rushing attempts.

Four of his nine completions went for touchdowns, and he sits atop the SEC leaderboard in passing touchdowns (20), yards per attempt (9.5) and passer rating (180.1). The Bulldogs don't need him to throw it 40 times per game to be effective with their running game and defense.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 28-of-38, 291 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 11 carries, -1 yard, 1 TD Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (SMU) Week 10 Outcome: Loss (28-51)

With an interception and a lost fumble, Ethan Grunkemeyer did not have his best individual performance of the season on Friday, but getting blown out 51-28 by SMU was a total team effort by the Hokies.

Despite the dud, he has still put together a terrific first season with Virginia Tech after transferring from Penn State during the offseason. His 71.7 percent completion rate ranks fifth among FBS quarterbacks, and he has 2,431 passing yards and 18 touchdowns with only three interceptions.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 20-of-31, 251 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 34 yards, 1 TD Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Texas A&M) Week 10 Outcome: Win (17-9)

After an 0-3 start to SEC play, South Carolina has won four in a row, and victories over Florida, Tennessee, Oklahoma and Texas A&M during that span have vaulted them to No. 20 in the AP poll.

LaNorris Sellers has 1,041 passing yards, 246 rushing yards and 15 total touchdowns during that four-game winning streak, and he led a pair of fourth-quarter scoring drives to turn a 9-7 deficit into a 17-9 victory.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 14-of-26, 177 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 20 carries, 89 yards, 2 TD Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (BYU) Week 10 Outcome: Win (28-20)

The Utes scored the first 14 points and the last 14 points of Saturday's marquee matchup against BYU, and while the offense stalled during BYU's run of 20 unanswered points, they still came out on top to improve to 9-0 on the year.

It was just the second time this season and first since Week 2 against Arkansas that Devon Dampier recorded multiple passing touchdowns and rushing touchdowns, and his 27 total scores this year are good for eighth on the FBS leaderboard.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 29-of-40, 319 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 1 carry, 3 yards Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Miami) Week 10 Outcome: Win (31-24)

By almost any measure, CJ Carr outperformed Heisman Trophy favorite Darian Mensah (24/43, 276 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT) in Saturday's marquee victory over No. 1 Miami to vastly improve Notre Dame's playoff outlook.

It was the first time this season that Carr has thrown for more than 300 yards, and with the Hurricanes defense slowing down the running game (29 carries, 93 yards), he stepped up in a big way.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 17-of-25, 182 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, 81 yards Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Georgia Tech) Week 10 Outcome: Win (44-17)

Louisville has won four in a row since a disappointing 2-3 start, and Lincoln Kienholz has piled up 882 passing yards, 236 rushing yards and 10 total touchdowns during that winning streak.

His 9.8 yards per attempt are tops in the ACC and fourth in the nation, and he has 25 total touchdowns with 14 passing and 11 rushing. The former Ohio State recruit has proven to be a great fit in Jeff Brohm's offensive scheme and one of the more productive transfer quarterbacks in the country.

Week 10 Passing Stats: 18-of-34, 170 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT Week 10 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, -12 yards Week 10 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Georgia) Week 10 Outcome: Loss (7-42)

Trinidad Chambliss has four touchdown passes and five interceptions over his last three games, and losses to Texas and Georgia during that stretch have effectively removed Ole Miss from the College Football Playoff conversation.

After throwing just three interceptions all season in 2025, Chambliss has struggled protecting the football while also seeing a dip in his completion percentage (66.1 to 62.7), yards per attempt (8.8 to 7.1) and passer rating (155.4 to 135.3).

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Rankings after Week 10
articles.summary: Before the showdown-filled slate arrived in Week 10, the Heisman Trophy had already undergone a major change.
articles.body:
Before the showdown-filled slate arrived in Week 10, the Heisman Trophy had already undergone a major change.

News broke of an injury sidelining Miami receiver Malachi Toney, who then needed surgery to address his ankle issue. His absence was certainly felt Saturday night when the Hurricanes lost to Notre Dame.

And that very matchup also served as a key moment for ND's CJ Carr.

Miami QB Darian Mensah, despite the loss in South Bend, is still a prime contender for the Heisman. Carr, though, is solidly in the race alongside him.

While the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State (+1500)

LaNorris Sellers, QB, South Carolina (+5500)

Sam Leavitt, QB, LSU : Now that LSU has dropped three games, Leavitt has reached a make-or-break moment. If the Tigers beat Texas and Tennessee over the next two weeks, expect Leavitt's stock to surge. With a loss in either tilt, however, he'll drift from the conversation.

Malachi Toney, WR, Miami : This is probably a final mention for Toney, who assembled an incredible two months. He'd dealt with on-and-off ankle problems all season, and an unfortunate injury led to him needing surgery. Miami is hoping Toney can return for the College Football Playoff, should the 'Canes make it.

Jesse Legree, WR, Oregon State : Legree has been fantastic, racking up 61 catches for 1,209 yards and 14 touchdowns—those last two totals both lead the FBS. Oregon State is now 5-4, though, with a trip to Boise State up next. Voters typically don't prioritize a player on a five-loss team, no matter his production.

DeSean Bishop, RB, Tennessee : Bishop, meanwhile, has been on a heater with five straight 100-yard performances. He just rushed for 109 yards and two scores in the rout of Kentucky, surpassing the 1,000-yard mark for the season. Tennessee heads to Texas A&M this weekend before hosting LSU. Two more victories for the Vols, and Bishop's candidacy may ascend. If not, never mind.

Jayden Maiava, QB, USC : Sitting at 2,524 yards with 20 touchdowns through the air, Maiava has decent numbers. USC, despite the noise, is 7-2 with a marquee trip to Indiana in Week 11 and to unbeaten UCLA in a couple weeks. Again, if the Trojans lose, write off Maiava. But his path to contention is evident.

Keelon Russell, QB, Alabama : In a battle of attrition, Russell is surviving thanks to Alabama's 7-2 record. He just threw for 206 yards and three touchdowns in a critical win at LSU, too. Since the Crimson Tide have a remaining slate of Vanderbilt, FCS team Chattanooga and rival Auburn, Russell is unlikely to win the Heisman but might snag a few votes if Bama finishes 10-2.

Nate Sheppard, RB, Duke : After a five-touchdown day against Boston College, Sheppard ripped apart NC State's defense for 217 yards and three scores. He ranks second and fourth in the nation, respectively, with 1,189 yards and 17 touchdowns on the ground. Week 11's trip to Miami is a decisive game for Sheppard and Duke.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State : Mestemaker has thrown for 2,962 yards and stands atop the FBS with 29 touchdown passes. That production has kept him in the conversation despite OSU's three losses, but on Saturday the Pokes host 8-1 Texas Tech. It's a huge opportunity—possibly good or bad—for the quarterback's award upside.

LaNorris Sellers, QB, South Carolina : Since a three-game skid earlier this season, South Carolina has rattled off four consecutive wins. Sellers has played an integral role in that streak, looking more like the dynamic dual-threat QB of his breakout 2024 campaign. He has passed for 2,100 yards, scampered for 637 and totaled 24 touchdowns for the 6-3 Gamecocks, who play at Arkansas this weekend.

Gio Lopez, QB, Wake Forest : The staff understandably sat Lopez due to a leg injury as Wake Forest cruised past FCS school Merrimack. Although he missed a valuable opportunity to pad his stats, Saturday's clash at SMU is far more important for the Demon Deacons' hopes of winning the ACC and making the CFP.

The cleanest path to the SEC Championship Game belongs to Georgia, the conference's only program with one league loss in 2026.

Gunner Stockton is a major beneficiary of that outlook.

As usual, his production is a bit behind other top contenders. He has thrown for 1,857 yards with 20 touchdowns to four interceptions, adding 233 yards and two scores as a runner. Not elite, but certainly good.

Beyond the Dawgs' 8-1 record, however, Stockton just helped himself immensely. He totaled 214 yards and five touchdowns in UGA's 42-7 walloping of Ole Miss.

Stockton is a tier or two below the next players, but he's firmly in the running as Missouri comes to town in Week 11.

Welcome to the spotlight, Devon Dampier.

For several weeks, we've highlighted Utah's quarterback as a player on the radar or just outside the Heisman Top 5. Dampier has routinely passed for 200-plus yards, made a notable impact as a runner and totaled three-ish touchdowns while helping the Utes remain unbeaten as a team.

Dampier lacked a signature moment on his résumé, however, preventing him from commanding more attention. That changed in a 28-20 triumph over BYU.

While throwing for 177 yards and two scores, Dampier added 87 yards and a pair of touchdowns on the ground. Plus, he impressively reeled in a contested 29-yard reception on a fourth-down trick play.

Dampier can bolster his appeal with a strong showing at Arizona this weekend, though a loss may nearly close any door to winning the Heisman.

The good news is Jeremiah Smith has continued to produce after a shoulder injury sidelined OSU quarterback Julian Sayin.

Smith corralled 10 passes for 83 yards and a touchdown at USC, then notched seven receptions for 133 yards and a score against Oregon. He's still an absolute weapon for the Ohio State offense.

The bad news is the Buckeyes lost both games.

Plenty of voters will recognize Smith's individual excellence and factor in Sayin's absence. At his current pace, Smith is still trending toward 85-plus catches with more than 1,500 yards and 15 touchdowns. That's a spectacular year.

Historically, though, team success is a real factor. If OSU loses a fourth game, choosing Smith as the winner would be a tough sell for many.

Shortly before halftime, CJ Carr scrambled right, turned to evade two Miami defenders, sprinted to the middle of the field and somehow found Aneyas Williams to convert a 3rd-and-4. Five plays later, Carr hit Micah Gilbert for a 17-yard touchdown that handed the Fighting Irish a 17-3 lead at halftime.

That moment is probably a bit underappreciated.

However, it was nothing short of essential in ND's 31-24 victory over top-ranked Miami. The game, as a whole, is now the selling point of Carr's candidacy.

Carr completed 29-of-40 passes for 319 yards with three touchdowns and zero turnovers. He's now thrown for 2,168 yards this season, totaling 24 scores to one interception while guiding ND to an 8-1 record.

Notre Dame hosts Boston College in Week 11, and a valuable game against a now-ranked SMU team looms afterward.

Had the Hurricanes not battled back in the second half at Notre Dame, we could be having a very different conversation.

During the first 30 minutes of Miami's first game without Toney, the 'Canes looked lost. The offensive line struggled, allowing constant pressure that limited Mensah's effectiveness. Notre Dame extended its lead to 24–3 early in the third quarter.

But a furious comeback eased the narrative around Mensah.

Ultimately, he finished 24-of-43 with 276 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. Mensah also put Miami in position to even the score, only for replay to determine Elija Lofton didn't quite complete his catch in the end zone.

Mensah's grip on the front-runner label is tenuous—Miami must avoid a second loss—but he remains a deserving pick with 2,831 yards and 30 touchdowns.

Duke, from which he transferred this offseason, is next for Mensah and the 'Canes.

articles.title: Aguirre busca la primera victoria del Valencia en Mestalla con todos los jugadores del primer equipo ante el Tavernes
articles.standfirst: El técnico mexicano reduce la presencia de canteranos en Copa por el compromiso del filial este miércoles ante el Cieza
articles.summary: El técnico mexicano reduce la presencia de canteranos en Copa por el compromiso del filial este miércoles ante el Cieza
articles.body: La Copa del Rey no dará tregua a ningún jugador del primer equipo del Valencia pese a la diferencia de nivel con el Tavernes, de la Lliga Comunitat (sexta categoría del fútbol español). Javier Aguirre ha incluido a la totalidad de futbolistas disponibles del primer equipo en la convocatoria para enfrentarse este martes al Tavernes, que ejercerá como local en Mestalla (21:00 horas) en la primera eliminatoria del torneo. La lista está marcada por la escasa presencia de jugadores del filial. El técnico ya explicó en la rueda de prensa previa que el Valencia Mestalla afronta dos compromisos importantes esta misma semana, uno aplazado el miércoles (ante el Cieza) que es el que ha provocado que no quiera trastocar los planes del técnico Óscar Sánchez. Por este motivo, Aguirre ha optado por recurrir mayoritariamente a futbolistas de la primera plantilla y limitar la participación de canteranos a los que ya están habitualmente en la dinámica del primer equipo, a excepción del lesionado Otorbi. Entre los nombres citados figuran habituales del primer equipo como Gayà -aunque confirmó que no iba a jugar de inicio, en la rueda de prensa previa- Pepelu, Javi Guerra, Hugo Duro, Sadiq, Luis Rioja, Maffeo, Copete, Tárrega o Danjuma. Lo normal es que el técnico dé minutos a aquellos futbolistas que menos están jugando desde que él llegó al banquillo del Valencia. Las principales ausencias obedecen a los compromisos internacionales de varios jugadores. El Valencia no puede contar con el portero Stole Dimitrievski, el delantero Aliou Dieng ni el defensa Mouctar Diakhaby, concentrados con sus respectivas selecciones durante este parón. La ausencia de los tres reduce las alternativas de Aguirre, especialmente en la portería, en la que podría debutar Van Oevelen. El encuentro, correspondiente a la primera eliminatoria de la Copa del Rey, se disputará este martes a las 21:00 horas en Mestalla, aunque con la Tavernes como equipo local. El Valencia, que no ha ganado ninguno de los siete partidos de Liga en casa esta temporada (dos empates y cinco derrotas). articles.title: La reacción de Balde al enterarse de que De Jong sería lateral en el Metropolitano
articles.standfirst: Unas imágenes de DAZN revelan cómo Flick preguntó al medio si podía jugar en la banda y cómo reaccionaron los jugadores en el banquillo
articles.summary: Unas imágenes de DAZN revelan cómo Flick preguntó al medio si podía jugar en la banda y cómo reaccionaron los jugadores del Barça en el banquillo
articles.body: La victoria del Barcelona frente al Atlético de Madrid dejó una de las imágenes más curiosas del encuentro en el Metropolitano. Hansi Flick volvió a demostrar que no tiene reparos a la hora de introducir cambios inesperados en el planteamiento táctico y sorprendió a propios y extraños al colocar a Frenkie de Jong como lateral derecho durante la segunda mitad. Una decisión que no solo llamó la atención del futbolista neerlandés, sino que también provocó reacciones entre los jugadores que estaban en el banquillo, especialmente Alejandro Balde. Unas imágenes captadas por DAZN permiten conocer cómo se desarrolló la conversación entre el entrenador alemán y el centrocampista antes de saltar al terreno de juego. Flick se acercó a De Jong para preguntarle si estaba dispuesto a ocupar la banda derecha. El jugador escuchó la propuesta, aceptó sin poner ningún impedimento y terminó mostrando una sonrisa ante la inesperada misión que le acababan de encomendar. La escena no terminó ahí. Mientras se preparaba para entrar, el neerlandés comentó a Gavi y Szczesny que su nueva posición sería la de lateral derecho. La noticia generó cierta incredulidad entre los futbolistas presentes. Tunkara incluso tuvo que explicarle a Alex Campos lo que estaba sucediendo, mientras Balde seguía atentamente la conversación. La reacción del lateral izquierdo azulgrana también resulta significativa. Balde, que atraviesa un periodo con escasa participación en los planes de Flick y que apunta a venta en enero, permaneció serio al conocer que De Jong sería el encargado de ocupar el carril derecho.
